01 · The idea

GSTV reaches people between decisions: out of the house, near the store, ready to act.

The current system is not broken, it is quiet. The refresh keeps the equity that matters, the logo and Montserrat, then gives the brand a wider palette, a single repeatable graphic device and a sense of movement. Same company, more voltage.

Attention, earned
We hold the only screen with no skip button. The brand should look as unmissable as the moment it owns.
Built to move
Audiences in motion, retailers nearby, action triggered. Motion is the through-line in colour, type and layout.
Clear, not corporate
Plain language and bold numbers. We say what we mean so partners can act fast.
02 · The constant: logo

The logo does not change.

It is the most recognised asset GSTV owns. The refresh protects it: approved lockups, fixed clear space and a clear set of don'ts.

03 · Secondary identity

The Droplet.

The teardrop inside the G, lifted out and redrawn with a softer body and a single tail to the lower left. One silhouette: a viewport that frames people, an outline that holds a stat and a marker that replaces the bullet point across decks.

The shapeOne silhouette, drawn once.
Photo viewportCrop imagery for hero moments and dividers.
Stat holderOutline to frame one proof point.
04 · Colour

Strong colour, used on purpose.

Two colours are locked to the logo and never change. Around them sits a vivid secondary set that gives the brand range: an electric lime and cyan for energy, a warm amber and coral for action. Cloud sits with navy and lime. Reach for amber and coral as accents, not wallpaper.

Midnight#141B2E · Primary dark, used most
Ink Navy#3E5170 · Cards, secondary surfaces
Brand Green#7FC678 · From the logo, used sparingly
Pulse Lime#B6F35A · Headlines accent, energy
Cyan Glow#1FC8C2 · Counter to lime, motion
Fuel Amber#FFB12E · Warm accent, agenda numerals
Spark Coral#FF6A5C · CTA, attention moments
Cloud#F4F1EC · Light surface, rare use
05 · Signature gradients

Three gradients, three jobs.

Gradients carry the energy where flat colour cannot. One for the hero, one for backgrounds and one for action moments. Used sparingly and in this order, they keep the brand consistent across surfaces.

MotionCyan to Lime · the hero
DepthMidnight to Navy · backgrounds
HeatOrange to Red · action moments

Suggested balance

A rough rule for any layout. Lots of dark foundation, a confident hit of brand green and lime, then small sparks of warmth.

Foundation 60 Brand 18 Lime 12 Heat 5 Cloud 5
06 · Typography

Montserrat, and only Montserrat.

One typeface across the whole system. It is geometric, confident and reads well at both huge display sizes and at body. Keeping it as the single voice removes the friction of pairing and forces hierarchy to come from weight, size and colour.

Montserrat
Primary · display, headlines, body, captions, numerals
Regular Medium SemiBold ExtraBold Black
Display and headlines
Aa Gg 0123

Black and ExtraBold for hero type and big stat numbers. SemiBold for sub-heads. Tighten tracking to minus two percent on large sizes so the letters lock together.

Body and UI
Aa Gg 0123

Montserrat Regular or Medium for body and interface, set at 16 to 18px with relaxed line height. Track at zero. The same typeface used carefully reads as deliberate, not monotonous.

07 · Typography in use
Recommendation

Use Montserrat more boldly.

The typeface is right. The way it is set today is the timid part. Current decks lean on lighter weights at modest sizes, so headlines do not land. The proposal: push Montserrat to ExtraBold and Black, set it larger, tighten the tracking and let it dominate the layout. Same font, far more presence.

Today
Customers in Motion
Montserrat SemiBold · modest size · reads as a label.
Proposed
Customers in Motion
Montserrat Black · oversized · tight tracking · reads as a statement.
08 · Voice and tone

Confident. Kinetic. Clear.

GSTV talks like the screen it owns: direct and full of energy, never showy. Short sentences. Real words. Big claims backed by a number, not by adjectives.

We sound like this
  • The only screen project cannot skip.
  • 115 million people, every month, in minutes.
  • Right message, right place, right moment.
  • Plain language. Proof you can act on.
We do not sound like this
  • Synergistic omni-channel solutions.
  • Unparalleled best-in-class ecosystems.
  • Long, hedged sentences full of qualifiers.
  • Hype with no number behind it.
09 · Imagery

Real people, in motion.

Photography decides whether the refresh feels premium or generic. Three routes sit on the table. The first is GSTV's existing library, shown as a baseline. The next two are the refresh proposals. Each holds one treatment consistently, never mixed inside a single deck.

01
Existing stockThe current library. Bright, friendly, commercial. Useful as a baseline.
02
Middle American & authenticWarm, natural, unposed. Real drivers and forecourts. Brand colour carried by type and the Droplet.
03
Bold & contemporaryHigh contrast, saturated, design-led. Studio composition. Reads premium and modern.
09a · Route 1

Existing stock · baseline

The current library. Bright, friendly and commercial. Does the job for routine slides but sits in the same visual lane as every other ad-tech deck, so it does little to lift the brand or earn a second look.

09b · Route 2

Middle American & authentic

Warm, natural and unposed. Real drivers, real forecourts, soft daylight. The brand colour is carried by type and the Droplet rather than by a photo treatment, so the imagery stays honest. Best where GSTV wants to feel close to its everyday audience.

09c · Route 3

Bold & contemporary

High contrast, saturated, design-led. Strong colour fields, studio composition and a graphic, unmissable feel. Signals a premium media platform rather than a utility. Best where GSTV is fighting for attention against social and streaming.

10 · Iconography

One family, three accent colours.

One weight, 2px rounded strokes. Lime or cyan on dark with amber for action moments. Built around the things GSTV talks about most: place, audience, screen, retail and proof.
